Senate AI Commission (chaired by Rolando Rodrigo Zapata Bello, PRI) confirms that the initiative is prepared for imminent presentation. Proposed institutional framework: national AI authority, certification system, mandatory registration of high-risk systems, national strategy with public funding. Principles: personal data protection, algorithmic non-discrimination, right to challenge automated decisions. Alignment with international standards.

Amendment to the Código Penal del Estado de México (Penal Code of the State of Mexico) approved by the LXII Legislatura (62nd Legislature). Adds article 211 Quinquies 1, imposing penalties of up to 5 years imprisonment and 500 UMAs (Unit of Measurement and Adjustment, ~$56,570 MXN) for the non-consensual generation or distribution of AI-manipulated sexual content (intimate deepfakes). The Article 73 reform initiative establishes a 180-day deadline for Congress to enact the Ley General de IA (General Law on Artificial Intelligence) once the reform enters into force. Official document verified in SIL (Legislative Information System), Secretaría de Gobernación.

The opinion on the Ley General de IA (General Law on Artificial Intelligence) was approved in Senate commissions on February 12, 2026. The plenary vote is scheduled for February 25. The opinion includes a risk-based approach (4 levels), creation of a national AI authority, Registro Nacional de Sistemas de IA (National Registry of AI Systems), and regulatory sandboxes. 72 experts participated in 6 discussion forums.
